social.title: Fiestas de Octubre at the Auditorio Benito Juárez
social.description: For one month the city throws itself a fair — palenque concerts, rides, and every antojito Jalisco makes, all on one hill.
social.bonus: Ride one thing that spins before eating, not after.

social.title: Sunday Morning Ballet Folclórico at the Degollado
social.description: The University of Guadalajara's folk ballet has owned Sunday mornings at the Teatro Degollado for decades — whirling jalisco skirts under a frescoed dome.
social.bonus: Sit close enough to hear the zapateado over the mariachi.

social.title: Winter Baseball with the Charros de Jalisco
social.description: Mexican Pacific League nights at the Panamericano are half baseball, half fiesta — bandas in the stands and micheladas by the litre.
social.bonus: Buy a stranger's section a round of peanuts.

social.title: Catch Atlas at the Estadio Jalisco
social.description: The 1970 and '86 World Cups played here — now it belongs to Atlas and the barra that never stops singing, in the city's great old concrete bowl.
social.bonus: Learn one chant well enough to join it.

social.title: Sunday Art Fair at Glorieta Chapalita
social.description: Every Sunday for sixty years local painters have ringed the Chapalita roundabout with canvases — coffee in hand, art on the grass, deals to be made.
social.bonus: Buy one piece under 200 pesos directly from the artist.

social.title: Dinner and Cumbia at El Parián de Tlaquepaque
social.description: The covered courtyard of El Parián in San Pedro Tlaquepaque turns every evening into an open-air party with roaming musicians, cold cheladas, and tables packed with locals letting loose.
social.bonus: Get up and dance in the central courtyard for at least one full song — no sitting it out.

social.title: Taco Crawl Through Colonia Mexicaltzingo
social.description: This working-class neighborhood east of the center is Guadalajara's unsung taco heartland, where carnitas, lonches, and guisados spill out of family kitchens onto the sidewalk.
social.bonus: Hit at least five different stalls and let the vendor at each one choose your order for you.

social.title: Lucha Libre Night at Arena Coliseo Guadalajara
social.description: Arena Coliseo has been hosting lucha libre since 1953 and on fight nights it erupts into one of the loudest, most theatrical spectacles in Mexican sports.
social.bonus: Buy a luchador mask from the vendors outside and wear it for at least two full matches inside the arena.

social.title: Salsa Night at La Bodeguita del Medio
social.description: This Cuban-flavored social club in Colonia Americana heats up after 10 pm with live bands, strong mojitos, and a dance floor that demands you participate.
social.bonus: Ask someone you don't know to teach you a salsa move — then actually use it before you leave.

social.title: Sunday Lunch at La Fonda de San Miguel
social.description: Set inside a gorgeous 17th-century ex-convent courtyard in the Historic Center, La Fonda de San Miguel serves Jaliscan classics that taste like they were cooked by someone's grandmother.
social.bonus: Order something off the menu you can't pronounce and ask the waiter to explain it before you eat.

social.title: Rooftop Sunset at Hotel Demetria
social.description: The rooftop bar at Hotel Demetria delivers panoramic views over Colonia Americana with some of the coldest cocktails in the city.
social.bonus: Strike up a conversation with a stranger at the bar and get a local restaurant recommendation you've never heard of.

social.title: Craft Beer Night at Cervecería Chapultepec
social.description: The bar that ignited Guadalajara's craft beer movement packs its long communal tables with students and creatives every night — loud, cheap, and completely unpretentious.
social.bonus: Challenge the table next to you to a round — loser buys the next pitcher.

social.title: Live Mariachi at Plaza de los Mariachis
social.description: The birthplace of mariachi as we know it erupts every evening with competing bands playing for tips, tables of mezcal, and visitors who came for one song and stayed for three hours.
social.bonus: Request a song, pay the musicians directly, and sing along — even if you don't know the words.

social.title: Bar-hop Calle Maestranza in the Historic Center
social.description: This one narrow pedestrian street in Centro packs cantinas that have been pouring mezcal and mariachi since the mid-20th century into a single electric block.
social.bonus: Walk into whichever cantina is loudest, sit at the bar, and order whatever the person next to you is drinking.

foodie.title: Oysters and Aguachile at La Docena
foodie.description: Guadalajara's great oyster bar — born here before it conquered the capital — runs on wood-fire, crushed ice, and the long lunch you meant to keep short.
foodie.bonus: Order one thing you can't pronounce.

foodie.title: Torta Ahogada from José el de la Bicicleta
foodie.description: The most famous torta stand in the city started on a bicycle and still drowns its birote in tomato and chile de árbol the same way — go before noon or go hungry.
foodie.bonus: Order it "bien ahogada" and don't reach for a fork.

foodie.title: Enchiladas at Restaurant El Sacromonte
foodie.description: A beloved Guadalajara landmark since 1978, El Sacromonte serves the city's definitive enchiladas tapatías — corn tortillas drenched in chile sauce, cream, and queso fresco in a colonial setting.
foodie.bonus: Order a second round of salsas and try every single one before touching your main dish.

foodie.title: Dinner at Alcalde Restaurante in Americana
foodie.description: Chef Francisco Ruano's tasting-menu temple in the Americana neighborhood redefines Jalisco ingredients with precision and restraint — one of the most important restaurants in Mexico right now.
foodie.bonus: Ask the sommelier to pair every course with something unexpected — tell them you trust them completely.

foodie.title: Tejuino and Elotes at Mercado Corona
foodie.description: Guadalajara's oldest functioning market pours its most essential street drink — tejuino, a fermented corn masa with lime sorbet — at counters that have been doing this for generations.
foodie.bonus: Pair your tejuino with a fully loaded elote and finish both before leaving the market floor.

foodie.title: Carne en su Jugo at Karne Garibaldi
foodie.description: Holder of a Guinness World Record for fastest restaurant service, this Guadalajara classic has been serving its legendary beef-and-bean broth since 1969 at unbeatable speed.
foodie.bonus: Time your order to the table — if it arrives in under 13 minutes, you've witnessed the record in action.

foodie.title: Breakfast at Café Madrid in the Historic Center
foodie.description: Open since 1936, this Guadalajara landmark serves chilaquiles and café de olla to politicians, artists, and early risers in a room that hasn't changed since your grandfather's era.
foodie.bonus: Sit at the counter, order the full desayuno completo, and read a physical newspaper — borrow one from another table.

foodie.title: Pozole at Restaurant Las 9 Esquinas
foodie.description: In a colonial courtyard tucked into one of Guadalajara's most photogenic neighborhood intersections, this kitchen serves the city's most comforting bowl of red pozole.
foodie.bonus: Load every single topping onto your bowl — tostadas, oregano, chile, cabbage — all of it, no restraint.

foodie.title: Eat Tortas Ahogadas at El Güero
foodie.description: Guadalajara's signature dish — a pork-stuffed birote roll drowned in fiery tomato-chile sauce — reaches its most uncompromising form at this decades-old stall near Mercado Medrano.
foodie.bonus: Order it 'bien picosa' — maximum chile — and finish the whole thing without reaching for water.

foodie.title: Drink Mezcal at La Fuente Cantina
foodie.description: One of the oldest cantinas in Centro — open since 1921 — La Fuente is all dark wood, taxidermied heads, and mezcal poured from unlabeled bottles by men who've worked here for decades.
foodie.bonus: Ask the bartender what the oldest mezcal in the house is, then order two glasses — one for you, one for whoever is sitting nearest.

foodie.title: Eat Birria at La Chata
foodie.description: Open since 1942, this Centro institution serves the definitive Guadalajara birria — dark, spiced, fall-apart goat in clay bowls that smell like the soul of Jalisco.
foodie.bonus: Order a second bowl without pausing — the señora will respect you for it.

chill.title: An Hour at the Museo de Arte de Zapopan
chill.description: MAZ puts serious contemporary art — Jalisco's best rotating shows — a plaza away from the basilica, and admission rarely costs more than the coffee after.
chill.bonus: Pick the one work you'd steal and defend the choice.

chill.title: Walk the Four Plazas to the Sunday Kiosco Band
chill.description: The Centro unfolds as a cross of plazas around the cathedral — end at Plaza de Armas, where the municipal band has played the iron kiosk on Sundays for over a century.
chill.bonus: Stay for three full songs at the kiosco.

chill.title: Find the Japanese Garden Inside Bosque Los Colomos
chill.description: Hidden in the city's eucalyptus forest is a koi-ponded Japanese garden gifted by sister-city Kyoto — the quietest place inside the ring road.
chill.bonus: Sit on one bench for fifteen unbroken minutes.

chill.title: Sit in the Reading Room of the Biblioteca Iberoamericana Octavio Paz
chill.description: Housed inside a 17th-century convent attached to the Universidad de Guadalajara, this library's main reading room — with its painted arches and courtyard fountain — is the most beautiful place in the city to do absolutely nothing urgent.
chill.bonus: Pull a book at random from the open stacks — read the first page out loud to yourself in a whisper.

chill.title: Stand Under the Vaults of the Templo Expiatorio
chill.description: Guadalajara's neo-Gothic masterpiece took 75 years to finish — come at dusk when the stained glass goes molten and the carillon plays from the tower.
chill.bonus: Stay for the carillon on the hour.

chill.title: Open-Air Concert at the Teatro Degollado Courtyard
chill.description: The neoclassical Teatro Degollado hosts free Sunday morning performances by the Jalisco Philharmonic Orchestra in its grand foyer and courtyard — one of the city's finest free rituals.
chill.bonus: Stay for the entire program without checking your phone once.

chill.title: Afternoon at the Planetario Severo Díaz Galindo
chill.description: Guadalajara's public planetarium in Huentitán runs Spanish-language dome shows on astronomy and the cosmos that are genuinely stunning and cost almost nothing.
chill.bonus: Ask the staff one question after the show that you couldn't answer yourself — then write down the answer.

chill.title: Afternoon at the Zoológico Guadalajara
chill.description: One of Mexico's oldest zoos, perched above the Barranca de Huentitán, houses over 2,000 animals and doubles as an unexpectedly scenic viewpoint over the canyon.
chill.bonus: Find the most obscure animal in the park that you couldn't name before arriving and look it up on the spot.

chill.title: Afternoon at Parque Agua Azul
chill.description: Guadalajara's grand central park has anchored the city since 1952 — its orchid house, butterfly pavilion, and shaded paths make it the rare urban green space that actually delivers.
chill.bonus: Visit the orchid house and find one species you've never seen before — remember its name without writing it down.

chill.title: Visit the Museo de las Artes (MUSA) at UdeG
chill.description: The University of Guadalajara's art museum holds stunning Orozco frescoes inside its main hall dome and rotates contemporary exhibitions that are consistently among the city's sharpest.
chill.bonus: Lie flat on your back on the museum floor under the dome fresco and look up for a full two minutes.

chill.title: Explore the Palacio de Gobierno and its Orozco Murals
chill.description: José Clemente Orozco's fire-breathing staircase mural of Miguel Hidalgo is one of the most viscerally powerful paintings in the Americas — and it's free to walk up and stand inside it.
chill.bonus: Stand at the exact center of the staircase under the mural for five full minutes without taking a photo.

chill.title: Browse Antiquities at Mercado de Antigüedades Agua Azul
chill.description: Beneath the shade of the Parque Agua Azul trees, weekend vendors spread out a sprawling treasure hunt of vintage ceramics, coins, and forgotten Jalisco relics.
chill.bonus: Negotiate at least one price down by 30% — in Spanish only.

chill.title: Sunset Drinks at the Terraza of Hotel Morales
chill.description: Perched above the historic center, this rooftop terrace on a 1907 building delivers panoramic spires-and-sunsets with a paloma in hand.
chill.bonus: Strike up a conversation with whoever is sitting alone at the bar — buy them one drink.

chill.title: Read in Parque Metropolitano de Guadalajara
chill.description: At 150 hectares, this is one of the largest urban parks in Latin America — and on a weekday morning it belongs almost entirely to joggers, old men playing chess, and whoever has the good sense to bring a book.
chill.bonus: Find the chess tables near the main fountain and challenge whoever is sitting there — you don't need to know how to play well.

chill.title: Sit in the Cathedral of Guadalajara at Dusk
chill.description: The twin yellow towers of this 1618 cathedral glow gold at sunset and the interior fills with incense smoke and the last of the day's light hitting the neoclassical altars.
chill.bonus: Find the mummified bishops displayed in the crypt — they're real and most visitors never find them.

adventure.title: Ride a Calandria Through the Centro Histórico
adventure.description: The carriages that have looped the Centro for a century are electric now — same routes, same stories from the drivers, no horse guilt.
adventure.bonus: Ask the driver for their favourite building and actually listen.

adventure.title: Climb the Round Pyramids of Guachimontones
adventure.description: An hour west sit the circular step pyramids of the Teuchitlán culture — a UNESCO site most visitors to Jalisco never hear about, ringed by agave hills.
adventure.bonus: Walk the largest circle twice — once fast, once slow.

adventure.title: Hunt Treasure at the Tonalá Tianguis
adventure.description: Every Thursday and Sunday the pottery capital turns its streets into one of Mexico's great open-air markets — ceramics, blown glass, and barro straight from the family workshops.
adventure.bonus: Haggle politely for one piece and get the maker's name.

adventure.title: Make the Pilgrimage to the Basílica de Zapopan
adventure.description: The 1690s basilica holds Jalisco's most venerated Virgin and a Wixárika art museum in its cloister — the plaza outside runs on birria and church bells.
adventure.bonus: Try a vampiro from a stand on the plaza afterward.

adventure.title: Get Lost in Barrio Analco
adventure.description: Guadalajara's oldest surviving neighborhood — predating the Spanish grid — is a dense tangle of baroque church facades, street murals, and corner tiendas that hasn't been gentrified yet.
adventure.bonus: Find the Templo de San Sebastián de Analco and ask the caretaker inside to show you the colonial-era paintings — they're almost never lit up for tourists.

adventure.title: Catch a Chivas Match at Estadio Akron
adventure.description: Club Deportivo Guadalajara — Chivas, the only top-flight Mexican club that only signs Mexican players — plays in a striking 49,000-seat stadium with supporters who treat the game as a religious event.
adventure.bonus: Buy a Chivas scarf from a street vendor outside and wear it in the general admission Norte section — sing every chant even if you don't know the words.

adventure.title: Stroll the Ajijic Malecón on Lake Chapala
adventure.description: An hour south, Mexico's largest lake laps at the cobbled malecón of Ajijic — mountain light, muraled streets, and a boardwalk built for doing nothing slowly.
adventure.bonus: Walk past the tourist malecón and find the fishermen's dock on the east side — ask to join a reed-boat launch for a few pesos.

adventure.title: Visit the Museo Regional de Guadalajara
adventure.description: Housed in a 17th-century Baroque seminary in Centro, this long-standing state museum holds pre-Hispanic artifacts, a woolly mammoth skeleton, and colonial-era paintings that most visitors walk past entirely.
adventure.bonus: Find the mammoth skeleton room and photograph it from the floor looking up — bring this back as your single best photo of the trip.

adventure.title: Hike the Cerro del Colli in Zapopan
adventure.description: This volcanic hill on the city's northwest edge is a proper trail — not a park walk — with panoramic views over the entire Guadalajara metro that reward anyone who actually pushes to the summit.
adventure.bonus: Start before 6 a.m. to summit at sunrise — the city lights fading below you as the sky turns pink is a completely different experience.

adventure.title: Watch a Charro Show at the Lienzo Charro de Jalisco
adventure.description: The official home of charrería — Mexico's equestrian rodeo tradition born in Jalisco — hosts Sunday competitions where horsemen in silver-studded suits perform feats that no arena in the world replicates.
adventure.bonus: Move down to ringside between rounds — nobody enforces the seating and the smell of horse and leather up close is the whole point.

adventure.title: Explore Tlaquepaque's Artisan Galleries
adventure.description: This village-absorbed-by-the-city has been Mexico's craft capital for decades, with genuine blown-glass studios, talavera workshops, and iron foundries on streets unchanged for generations.
adventure.bonus: Enter a working glass-blowing studio on Independencia and ask to watch a piece being made — most will say yes.

adventure.title: Day Trip to Tequila Town and the Agave Fields
adventure.description: An hour northwest, the blue agave landscape that inspired a UNESCO designation rolls out around the white-walled town where the spirit was born and still lives.
adventure.bonus: Skip the tourist distilleries and walk into a small family taberna on the outskirts — ask for a taste straight from the still.

adventure.title: Explore the Instituto Cultural Cabañas
adventure.description: José Clemente Orozco's apocalyptic murals cover the domed chapel of a 200-year-old UNESCO World Heritage hospice in the most confrontational art you'll see in Mexico.
adventure.bonus: Lie flat on the floor directly under the central dome and stare up at the Man of Fire for a full minute without looking away.

adventure.title: Wander the Mercado Libertad (San Juan de Dios)
adventure.description: Latin America's largest covered market swallows you whole with three floors of birria stalls, leather goods, herbs, and Jalisco kitsch dating back to 1958.
adventure.bonus: Find a stall selling tejuino and drink the whole cup standing at the counter without adding extra lime.

adventure.title: Hike the Barranca de Huentitán
adventure.description: Guadalajara's secret canyon drops 600 meters into a raw gorge where the Santiago River carves through volcanic rock and nobody talks about it enough.
adventure.bonus: Reach the river at the bottom and touch the water — don't turn back at the viewpoint like everyone else.

active.title: Watch the Sunrise from Cerro de la Reina in Tonalá
active.description: The small hill overlooking Tonalá's craft district rewards the 20-minute climb with a panorama over red-roofed workshops and, on clear mornings, a distant silhouette of Volcán de Colima.
active.bonus: Be at the summit before 6:30 a.m. — photograph the exact moment the sun clears the horizon.

active.title: Mountain Bike the Bosque de la Primavera Trails
active.description: The pine and oak forest west of the city harbors a network of red-dirt singletracks that tapatío riders treat as their personal backyard.
active.bonus: Ride at least 20 km without turning back early — take a photo at the furthest point to prove it.

active.title: Run the Bosque Los Colomos Trails at Dawn
active.description: This 90-hectare urban forest in Zapopan opens before sunrise and rewards early runners with misty cedar paths, birdsong, and zero crowds — the city's best-kept athletic secret.
active.bonus: Run the full outer loop — approximately 5km — without stopping, then find the Japanese garden at the end.

active.title: Evening Walk Along Paseo Chapultepec
active.description: Guadalajara's most elegant boulevard fills at dusk with joggers, vendors, and couples — a living cross-section of the city at its most unhurried and charming.
active.bonus: Stop at a street cart and eat something you've never tried before — ask the vendor what their personal favorite is.

active.title: Cycle the Vía RecreActiva on Sunday
active.description: Every Sunday morning Guadalajara shuts down 55 kilometers of streets and hands them to cyclists, skaters, and joggers in one of the world's great urban bike rituals.
active.bonus: Rent a bike at Glorieta Minerva and ride all the way to Parque Agua Azul without stopping — no shortcuts.
